Timeline::tz_localize¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::tz_localize(std::string_view tz_name, int fold = 0, std::string_view nonexistent = "raise") -> Timeline

What It Does¶

Attaches timezone meaning to local wall-clock timestamps and converts them into real UTC-backed instants under that timezone.

This is not the same as tz_convert():

  • tz_localize(...) Says what timezone the stored wall-clock values should be interpreted in.

  • tz_convert(...) Re-views already-defined instants in another timezone.

Parameters¶

tz_name

The timezone whose wall-clock rules should be applied.

fold

Controls ambiguous repeated local times during fall-back transitions.

  • 0 Prefer the earlier interpretation.

  • 1 Prefer the later interpretation.

Most ordinary timestamps are not ambiguous, so this mainly matters around DST fall-back hours.

nonexistent

Controls how nonexistent local wall-clock times should be handled.

  • "raise" Treat the impossible local time as an error.

The current implementation exposes the policy parameter even when your concrete example does not trigger it.

Returns¶

Timeline A timezone-aware timeline.

Examples¶

Example 1. Interpret stored wall-clock values as New York local time.

auto out = local_wall.tz_localize("America/New_York");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[2], tz=America/New_York)
[ 2024-11-01 09:00:00, 2024-11-01 10:15:30 ]

Notes¶

  • tz_localize() changes the underlying instant because it reinterprets local wall-clock values.

  • Use fold and nonexistent intentionally around DST boundary work.
